reviews.frank_statement: Model output/semantic intent must not itself confer execution authority; effects cross an independently enforced capability/commit boundary.
reviews.counterhypothesis: A simpler trusted local runtime could safely treat validated model-emitted tool calls as sufficient authority, making capability tokens redundant overhead.
reviews.falsifier: Adversarial Harness testing demonstrates no authority escalation, destructive-equivalent bypass or resource-scope violation under direct validated model-call authority across the required system-effect suite.
independent_checks: Project-Frankenstein historical safety/authority failure lineage contains approval-bypass and capability-scoping negative evidence mapped into current BASE/Harness acceptance.
WASI/Component Model independently separates imported host interfaces/resources from component code and uses typed boundary contracts rather than text naming as authority.
adversarial_checks: Treat textual capability/resource names as forged authority; attempt scope widening and destructive-equivalent host paths.
reviews.reason: Survives independent project-history negative evidence and an external typed-capability architecture analogue. This supports the separation principle, not any particular token format as uniquely optimal.
reviews.claycode_action: Retain model_intent_and_effect_authority_separate and capability-bearing effect lowering; do not let parser convenience collapse authority into syntax.

reviews.frank_statement: Adaptive user-specific visual learner state must be representable/replayable in ClayCode without becoming semantic truth or execution authority.
reviews.counterhypothesis: Generic G9 records/deltas are insufficient for calibrated open-set online-learning lifecycle semantics, requiring a new dedicated language primitive.
reviews.falsifier: An executable H1 learner transition cannot be represented with deterministic version/provenance/admission/promotion/rollback semantics using the current generic IR.
independent_checks: Current G9 generic records include Delta, evidence/provenance refs, epochs, statuses, budgets and RecoveryRef-compatible rollback hooks; this is representability analysis, not live learner evidence.
adversarial_checks: Feature-version migration, rejected pseudo-labels, candidate rollback, UNKNOWN/CONFLICT routing and over-budget pause.
reviews.reason: No executable H1 Micro Visual Classifier state machine was available in this run, so generic representability remains a working hypothesis rather than independently validated FRANK-to-ClayCode adequacy.
reviews.claycode_action: Do not add visual-learning syntax now; require a concrete H1 counterexample before semantic change.

reviews.frank_statement: ClayCode must carry semantic dependency/coupling information sufficient for automatic incremental UnifiedDB/ClayGraph maintenance instead of forcing full hot-path search/reconstruction.
reviews.counterhypothesis: Runtime observation alone can maintain the needed graph/database dependencies; compiler-emitted signatures are unnecessary duplication.
reviews.falsifier: Matched incremental-service tests show no correctness, latency, invalidation or drift advantage from compiler-derived signatures over runtime-only dependency tracking.
independent_checks: Current UnifiedDB/ClayGraph schemas already contain epochs, deltas, projection receipts and invalidation structures independent of ClayCode prose.
MLIR independently demonstrates extensible typed dialect/interface IR with explicit parsers/verifiers/canonicalization, supporting separation of semantic IR from surface syntax.
adversarial_checks: Dynamic dispatch/FFI dependency absent statically; stale compiler signature; runtime-only dependency discovered after canonicalization.
reviews.reason: Compiler-derived signatures are justified as one source, but must be fused with runtime receipts rather than treated as complete dependency truth.
reviews.claycode_action: Design signatures as compiler products plus runtime reconciliation/invalidation, not a second authoritative hand-written graph.
